questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear gear that helps other drivers see you and your motorcycle. Bright, reflective clothing makes you easier to spot.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should wear a jacket:

options.text: No matter what the weather is.
Only if you will ride for more than half an hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter what the weather is.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you from the sun and helps prevent dehydration.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is safer than listening to music.

questions.explanation: Wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Honk your horn and make rude gestures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let a tailgater pass. Speeding up will cause them to tailgate at a higher speed, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume they have ridden a motorcycle before.
Not assume they have ridden before and explain what to do.
Not explain anything because they are just a passenger.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume they have ridden before and explain what to do.
questions.explanation: Your passenger needs to know how to stay safe. Never assume they know what to do. Give them full instructions before every ride.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps you be seen at any time. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wear bright clothing whenever you ride.

questions.question: In a no passing zone:

options.text: A motorcycle may still pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if the pass is quick.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: No passing zones mean no passing for any vehicle, including motorcycles. Do not pass by riding off the roadway either.

questions.question: You should keep a safe distance behind other vehicles:

options.text: To give you time and space to see hazards and react.
So traffic counters can count you.
To encourage other drivers to cut you off.

questions.correctAnswerText: To give you time and space to see hazards and react.
questions.explanation: A safe distance gives you room to stop or move if the vehicle ahead stops suddenly. It also helps you see road hazards like potholes.

questions.question: A face shield:

options.text: Does not work as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, impact-resistant face shield provides the best protection for your eyes and face. Regular eyeglasses or sunglasses are not enough protection.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely to happen to:

options.text: Those who know their motorcycle well.
Those who have taken a safety course.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to new riders who do not have experience and do not know their motorcycle.

questions.question: What is NOT required to get a motorcycle license?
questions.explanation: To get a motorcycle license, you need a vision test, a test on road signs, a written test, and a riding skills test.

questions.question: Shifting into a lower gear has an effect similar to:
questions.explanation: Shifting your motorcycle into a lower gear slows you down, similar to applying the brakes. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: The only way to remove alcohol from your body is through:
questions.explanation: Only time allows your body to remove alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should only be done on long trips.
Should be part of your normal routine.
Are not helpful because you cannot change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of your normal routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of your regular riding routine. Also check them before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: Wearing reflective clothing is a good idea:
questions.explanation: Always wear reflective and bright clothing when riding a motorcycle. Crashes happen both during the day and at night, so wear highly visible clothing at all times.

questions.question: When approaching a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb the impact. This reduces the chance that the bump will throw you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: When choosing footwear, pick shoes that:

options.text: Have long laces that hang loose.

questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are tall and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be short so they don't catch on things. Tuck in laces so they cannot catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Goggles will:

options.text: Work as well as a face shield.
Give the same protection as a windshield.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes only, not your whole face. A face shield protects your entire face and is better than goggles. A windshield does not provide enough protection.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, the laces:
questions.explanation: Tuck in your shoelaces securely so they cannot catch on your motorcycle.

questions.question: The best lane position is the one that:

options.text: Allows you to draft off other vehicles.
Allows other motorists to see you.
Places you in other vehicles' blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allows other motorists to see you.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and lets them see you. It should help you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. A good position discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if something goes wrong.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of crashing?

options.text: Make sure other drivers can see you.
Hide your plans from other drivers.
Stay within one foot of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What is another name for shifting to a lower gear?
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear creates a braking effect. This is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: Most crashes happen in daylight. What should you wear to be more visible?
questions.explanation: Since most crashes happen in daylight, always wear bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: How should a motorcyclist choose their lane position?

options.text: Pick one spot in the lane and stay there all the time.
Weave between lane positions to keep other drivers out.
Change position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: What is an advantage of smoothly downshifting on a motorcycle?

options.text: It allows you to use engine braking.
You should not do it around other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to use engine braking.
questions.explanation: Downshifting smoothly can help you slow down using engine braking. If you use engine braking, tap your brake light separately so other drivers know you are slowing down.
